summary: iter98: Verified (1) Admin Lifetime Access section — list, search+grant, and Remove flow all work; Remove on web is immediate (no native Alert) and row disappears from list. (2) Home ActivityBanner in a 2-member household — banner shows 'N new or updated items' listing competition + event with actor name and 'Owner A added this'; tapping an activity-item-<id> navigates to the item and removes it from the banner on return; Mark all seen clears everything and persists across reload. (3) Solo household (applereview) dashboard renders with NO activity-banner and no errors. All 3 test cases PASS.
critical_code_review_comments: ActivityBanner (/app/frontend/src/components/ActivityBanner.tsx): schedule item is routed to /schedule/new?id=<id> — the schedule 'new' route acts as edit-when-id-provided, works today, but semantically odd (routing to a screen literally named 'new' to view an event). Not blocking; consider a dedicated schedule/[id].tsx in a future pass.

AdminScreen (/app/frontend/app/admin/index.tsx, 275 lines): getting close to the split-threshold; the four sections (analytics, testing, generate codes, search/grant, codes list, lifetime access) could each be extracted into small components for readability.
seed_data_creation: Created two fresh test users (iter98_ownera_<ts>@example.com / iter98_memberb_<ts>@example.com, password Test2026Pass!) via /app/backend/tests/setup_iter98_household.py; joined them into one household; created a competition (ITER98 State Championship) and a schedule event (ITER98 Practice) by A. Also revoked+re-granted lifetime for applereview@cheerplanner.app during admin test — final state has applereview back on the lifetime list (as originally seeded).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend endpoints used for setup: POST /api/auth/signup, /api/household/invite, /api/household/join, /api/competitions, /api/schedule, GET /api/activity. Admin testIDs: admin-search, lifetime-row-<user_id>, lifetime-revoke-<user_id>. Banner testIDs: activity-banner, activity-item-<resource_id>, activity-mark-all, activity-toggle-more (only shown when >3 items). Web build correctly bypasses native Alert on revoke (immediate confirm). The banner only appears in multi-member households and never for the actor's OWN edits — confirmed by solo test on applereview and by A never seeing his own edits.
